Psychological Assessment & Tests

How psychological assessment is done — interviews, observation, tests and what nurses should know.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • List methods of psychological assessment
  • Describe what IQ and personality tests measure
  • State the nurse's role in referral and observation

In simple words

Psychological assessment gathers information about a person’s thinking, feeling and behaviour to understand problems and plan help. It uses interviews, observation, questionnaires and standard tests.

Nurses do not diagnose mental illness — they observe, record, report and refer to the psychologist or psychiatrist. They also support patients through testing.

Assessment methods

Method What it is
Interview Talking to learn about history, feelings and problems
Observation Watching behaviour, mood and appearance
Questionnaire Standard written questions
Psychological test Standard tool measuring a specific ability or trait

Common tests

  • IQ tests — measure general intellectual ability (verbal and performance).
  • Personality tests — measure traits such as anxiety, introversion or emotional stability.
  • Projective tests — ambiguous stimuli (inkblots, pictures) reveal inner conflicts.
  • Neuropsychological tests — memory, attention and brain function.

A good test is reliable (consistent results) and valid (measures what it claims).

Nurse’s role

  • Observe and record behaviour accurately.
  • Note mood, speech, sleep, appetite and social contact.
  • Report changes to the doctor or psychologist.
  • Support the patient before and after tests.
  • Maintain confidentiality.

🔴 Nurse's boundary

Nurses observe, record, report and refer — they do not diagnose. Psychological diagnosis is made by the doctor or psychologist.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Admission assessment — note mood, behaviour, sleep and any psychiatric history.
  • Daily observation — record changes in behaviour, speech or appearance.
  • Support during testing — explain what will happen and reduce anxiety.
  • Confidentiality — share information only with the care team and with consent.
  • Referral — tell the doctor about concerning signs such as withdrawal, agitation or hopelessness.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Psychological assessment uses interview, observation, questionnaires and tests.
  2. IQ tests measure general intellectual ability.
  3. Personality tests measure traits such as anxiety and emotional stability.
  4. A good test is reliable (consistent) and valid (measures what it claims).
  5. Nurses observe, record, report and refer — they do not diagnose.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Projective tests use ambiguous stimuli such as inkblots.
  2. Neuropsychological tests check memory, attention and brain function.
  3. Confidentiality is essential in psychological assessment.
  4. Report behaviour changes to the doctor or psychologist.

📌 Memory trick

Nurse’s role in four Rs: Observe, Record, Report, Refer.

60-second revision

  • Assessment = interview + observation + questionnaires + tests.
  • IQ = intellectual ability; personality = traits.
  • Reliable = consistent; valid = measures what it claims.
  • Projective tests = inkblots/pictures.
  • Nurse: observe, record, report, refer; do not diagnose.

Test yourself

IQ tests mainly measure:

Answer: B. IQ tests measure general intellectual ability, including verbal and performance skills.

A good psychological test must be:

Answer: A. Reliability means consistent results; validity means it measures what it claims.

A projective test uses:

Answer: B. Projective tests present ambiguous stimuli so the person projects inner feelings.

The nurse's role in psychological assessment is to:

Answer: B. Nurses observe, record, report and refer; diagnosis is made by the doctor or psychologist.

Confidentiality in assessment means:

Answer: B. Information is shared only with the care team and with the patient's consent.
